The test image shows a corn ear with dark green mold growing over much of the kernels. Key features:
- Affected part: ear (kernels)
- Color: dark green mold covering kernels
- Pattern: mold covering a large portion of the ear

Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Trichoderma** (dark green mold on kernels) and **Ear_rots_Aspergillus** (olive-green to gray-green mold). Let me view reference images.
The Trichoderma reference images show dark green mold between/on yellow kernels — very similar to the test image. Let me check a few more candidates to be thorough.
Diplodia shows white/tan mold, Gibberella shows pinkish mold — neither matches the dark green in the test image. Let me view two more to complete my budget.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Corn ear with dark green mold covering much of the kernel surface, growing between kernels on an otherwise yellow ear. The mold has a characteristic deep forest/teal-green color.
- **Trichoderma reference**: Identical appearance — dark green mold growing between yellow kernels, covering large portions of the ear. Perfect match.
- **Aspergillus**: Olive-green to gray-green powdery mold, typically at the tip — different color and distribution.
- **Diplodia**: White/tan mold starting at the base — no green color.
- **Gibberella**: Pink/red mold at tip — no green color.
- **Fusarium**: White/pink/salmon cottony mold — no green.
- **Common_smut**: Fleshy white/black galls — completely different.

The dark green mold distributed across the kernels matches Ear_rots_Trichoderma precisely.
